Author: Sanjay Kumar Singh

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 40268 of 2022
Applicant :- Vinod Kumar

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Pawan Kumar Patel,Hemant Kumar Srivastava Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State and perused the record.

By means of this application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant Vinod Kumar, who is involved in Case Crime No. 318 of 2021, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, police station Chopan, district Sonebhadra, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.

As per prosecution case, in brief, informant, who is brother of the deceased, lodged the first information report on 05.12.2021 with regard to an incident which took place on 08.09.2021 against present applicant Vinod Kumar, Rajendra and Ukendra, who are husband and brothers-in-law of the deceased, with the allegation inter alia that marriage of his sister Saroja Devi @ Vineeta was solemnized with the present applicant five years ago and from their wedlock, one daughter and one Vinod Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117473257/
1 son, namely, Lali and Lala were born, who are presently aged about 3 and 1-1/2 years, respectively.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: F.I.R. further alleges that after two years of their marriage, the applicant started demanding Rs. 1 lac and one motorcycle whereas sufficient dowry was given by him in the marriage of his sister.
Since he is a poor person, he could not satisfy the aforesaid demand of the accused persons.

On 10.09.2021,
village pradhan gave information about murder of his sister on 08.09.2021 to his another sister Sunaida Devi.
On receiving said information, he went to the house of his sister and came to know that the applicant alongwith co-accused after committing murder of his sister ran away from there.
It is argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case.
After culmination of investigation, co-accused Rajendra and Ukendra have been exonerated and charge-sheet has been submitted only against the present applicant Vinod Kumar.
It is also submitted that marriage of the applicant with the deceased was a love-marriage, therefore, there was no question of demand of any dowry and the deceased died by committing suicide.
In the post mortem report, cause of death of the deceased found to be ante mortem hanging.
The applicant does not have any criminal history to his credit.
Lastly, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that there is no chance of the applicant fleeing away from the judicial process or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 28.03.2022 and in case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and cooperate with the trial.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State vehemently opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant by contending that the deceased died her unnatural death in her matrimonial home within five years of her marriage.
Referring to the post mortem report, it is also pointed out that time since death of the deceased is about three days, which corroborates the prosecution case.

It is also pointed out that neither the applicant gave any information about death of his wife to the police nor to her family members which shows his ulterior motive and the said conduct of the applicant cannot said to be a normal conduct of a human-being.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find that the deceased died her unnatural death within seven years of the her marriage in her matrimonial home,
therefore, presumption under Section 113B of the Indian Evidence Act shall be drawn against the applicant.
The applicant being husband was not only responsible for the safety and welfare of his wife, but is also under heavy onus to explain her unnatural death, which took place in his own house.
The further details relating to the incident need not be referred to herein since the allegations and the defence thereto is still open to be urged by the parties in the trial Court.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case as well as keeping in view the submissions advanced on behalf of parties, gravity of offence, role assigned to applicant and severity of punishment, I do not find any good ground to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is rejected.

It is made clear that the observation contained in the instant order is confined to the issue of bail and shall not affect the merit of the trial.
